not_verified: One boxwood density (670 kg/m^3) serves both armies; real ebony pieces would be denser
Pieces are fixed instances on their squares, not mated; no mid-game poses modelled
Knight head is a flat-sided extruded silhouette, not a carved solid
Turned profiles are polylines, so curved surfaces are fine conical bands

Running `ryucad check` inside this repo adds 4 warnings about the parent checkout's missing ryucad git drivers/hooks (.gitattributes, merge driver, pre-commit hooks) - a property of the repo, not the model; the quoted check result is the model's own
one_line: A Staunton-style chess set in starting position: six piece types as revolved lathe profiles (knight head an extruded silhouette), a 65-solid board, and 32 pieces coloured per assembly occurrence, ivory against ebony.
poses: starting position: both armies on ranks 1-2 and 7-8, knights facing the opposing army
exploded 'lift': white pieces +70 mm, black pieces +150 mm (images/detail.png)
specs: Board 392 x 392 x 16 mm mahogany base with 64 separate 42 mm square solids, maple #e8d5b5 / walnut #7a4a2b, a1 dark and queens on their colour
King 64 mm tall (30 mm base), queen 55.6 mm, bishop 49.5 mm, knight 51.5 mm, rook 38 mm, pawn 32 mm
Piece details as features: rook battlements from two crossed slot cuts, bishop mitre a diagonal slot cut, queen coronet of 8 cones + sphere finial, king cross, knight eyes a through-hole
Total mass 1.970 kg, volume 3,066,264 mm^3 (boxwood 670 kg/m^3 pieces, walnut 640 kg/m^3 board)
Exploded view 'lift' saved: white army +70 mm, black army +150 mm
title: Staunton chess set — ivory and ebony
